title: Osireion
visualBrief: Standing Osireion open megalithic hall/excavation: two rows of five massive plain square granite piers with worn bases/fractured surviving heights, incomplete longitudinal lintels and loose cap blocks. Coursed perimeter masonry with recessed rectangular door/niche bays, exposed central wet stone island/rectangular floor recesses and shallow opaque green-water moat in the pictured low-water state. Narrow timber side stair/bridge with simple rails. Complete opaque excavation floor and fitted retaining/earth rim meet a bounded mapped ground opening. No intact ancient roof, covered underground rooms/long passage, copied relief/graffiti or neighboring Seti I temple reconstruction.

Anchor heading0/native east-south; internal long axis-.97476887509rad points NE toward independently mapped Seti I temple, which remains untouched. Two five-pier rows are parallel to that axis. Signed bridge, recess and surviving-lintel allocation is picture-led and may be reversed by180degrees despite its fixed mapped long axis; mapped outline is an archaeological extent, not a measured pier/foundation plan. No PMTiles building shell corresponds to Osireion; replace none.
sourceFacts.architecturalHeights: Picture/map estimates: occupied low-water island22.5x10.2m, floor-5.45m relative to coarse anchor datum, excavation bed-6.3m, shallow water-5.5m. Ten square piers approximately2.4m across and3.5-4.2m tall, uneven broken tops, incomplete1m-deep longitudinal lintels. Main chamber outer28x21m/perimeter wall1.4m thick with three end recesses/five side bays. Outer excavation39x31.3m follows mapped envelope; perimeter meets retained6m terrain. Missing roof/covered subterranean chambers are not restored. Absolute pit depth, low/high-water levels, hidden foundations, exact surviving lintel/block inventory and stair engineering remain visualization estimates.
